words.def: to tell someone that you are disappointed in what they did
words.ex: Mom did not reproach me, but her look said enough.

words.def: expressed so clearly that it is easy to follow
words.ex: The scientist gave a lucid explanation of black holes.

words.def: an illness or disease
words.ex: The doctor could not identify the strange malady.

words.def: able to be understood in more than one way
words.ex: The ambiguous sign confused the drivers.

words.def: an image, idea or symbol that repeats throughout a story
words.ex: Birds are a motif that appears in every chapter of the novel.

words.def: to make someone nervous and confused
words.ex: Loud cheering can fluster a young speller.

words.def: to secretly steal money you were trusted to manage
words.ex: The treasurer tried to embezzle money from the club's account.

words.def: false spoken statements that damage someone's good name
words.ex: Spreading lies about a classmate is slander.

words.def: to rise and fall again and again
words.ex: Prices for fresh fruit fluctuate with the seasons.

words.def: too lively or cheerful to be held back or kept quiet
words.ex: Her irrepressible laughter soon had the whole class giggling.

words.def: to stun or amaze someone so much that they cannot think clearly
words.ex: The magician's final trick will stupefy even the grown-ups.

words.def: to copy someone else's words or ideas and pretend they are your own
words.ex: It is dishonest to plagiarize an essay from the internet.

words.def: to attack fiercely with blows or with words
words.ex: Critics began to assail the new plan as soon as it was announced.

words.def: a question, especially one asking for information
words.ex: The librarian answered my query about where to find maps.

words.def: to show that something is not valid or correct
words.ex: One wrong measurement can invalidate the whole experiment.

words.def: a person who always says something will not work
words.ex: The naysayer insisted our lemonade stand would fail.

words.def: done too quickly and carelessly
words.ex: Her slapdash book report was full of spelling errors.

words.def: to spoil how something looks by marking or damaging its surface
words.ex: It is against the law to deface a public building with graffiti.

words.def: big, strong and muscular
words.ex: The brawny farmer lifted the hay bale with ease.

words.def: to quench a thirst or satisfy a desire
words.ex: Cold water from the spring will slake your thirst.

words.def: a mix of two different kinds of things
words.ex: A mule is a hybrid of a horse and a donkey.

words.def: harm or damage done to someone or something
words.ex: Staying up late every night works to the detriment of your health.

words.def: not discouraged or made afraid by danger or difficulty
words.ex: Undaunted by the rain, the runners kept going.

words.def: starting and stopping again and again; not steady
words.ex: After the storm woke him twice, he had only a fitful sleep.

words.def: to wave something around in a threatening or showy way
words.ex: The actor will brandish a wooden sword during the play.

words.def: the best or most favorable possible
words.ex: Early morning is the optimal time to water a garden.

words.def: a huge flood or an overwhelming amount of something
words.ex: After the announcement, the office received a deluge of phone calls.

words.def: quietly thinking about something, often in a slightly sad way
words.ex: She gazed out the window with a pensive look.

words.def: too bold in taking things for granted or acting without permission
words.ex: It was presumptuous to invite yourself to their party.

words.def: a filthy, wretched condition caused by neglect or poverty
words.ex: The missionaries found families living in squalor near the dump.

words.def: to stick out from a surface
words.ex: A rusty nail began to protrude from the old board.

words.def: to officially approve an agreement or plan
words.ex: The states had to ratify the new plan before it became law.

words.def: ordinary and dull; part of everyday life
words.ex: Folding laundry is a mundane chore.

words.def: making people feel love or affection
words.ex: The puppy had an endearing way of tilting its head.

words.def: long and careful thought or discussion before a decision
words.ex: After hours of deliberation, the jury reached a verdict.

words.def: a written note or message, especially in an office
words.ex: The manager sent a memorandum about the new holiday schedule.

words.def: to use up most or all of a supply
words.ex: A long, hot hike can deplete the water in your bottle quickly.

words.def: loud fun and laughter
words.ex: The puppy's tumble down the slide caused great hilarity.

words.def: a person or thing that is mysterious and hard to understand
words.ex: The locked room in the attic was an enigma to the whole family.

words.def: long and difficult to get through, like a hard journey
words.ex: The pioneers made an arduous journey across the mountains.

words.def: firm and loyal; not changing
words.ex: He was a steadfast friend through every hard time.

words.def: holding on firmly and refusing to give up
words.ex: The tenacious puppy would not let go of the rope.

words.def: wanting to hurt someone back for a wrong they did
words.ex: The vindictive character spent years plotting to get even.

words.def: to pull something away from someone with a strong twist
words.ex: The toddler tried to wrest the toy from his brother's hands.

words.def: to hold someone's full attention as if under a spell
words.ex: The fireworks seemed to mesmerize the little children.

words.def: to give out a set amount to each person or purpose
words.ex: The teacher will allot ten minutes for each speech.

words.def: a short, clever, funny remark
words.ex: Dad made a quip about the burnt toast that made us all laugh.

words.def: very upsetting and frightening to go through
words.ex: The sailors told a harrowing story about the storm at sea.

words.def: to echo again and again
words.ex: The drums reverberate through the empty gym.

words.def: to please someone or give them a feeling of satisfaction
words.ex: It will gratify the coach to see us practice without being told.

words.def: slow and clumsy because of great weight, or dull and labored in style
words.ex: The ponderous elephant moved slowly down the riverbank.

words.def: a mistaken belief or a flaw in reasoning
words.ex: It is a fallacy that a person who is good at math cannot be good at art.

words.def: to prove that a statement or argument is wrong
words.ex: She used survey data to refute the claim that the new rule was unpopular.

words.def: shrewd and careful, especially with money or decisions
words.ex: The canny shopper waited for the sale before buying a coat.

words.def: to soak something completely
words.ex: The heavy rain will saturate the soccer field.

words.def: far more of something than is needed
words.ex: A glut of zucchini meant we gave bags of it to every neighbor.

words.def: to cut short or reduce something
words.ex: The storm forced us to curtail our trip.

words.def: to tease someone with something they want but cannot have yet
words.ex: The smell of cookies will tantalize us until dinner is over.

words.def: lasting only a short time
words.ex: The rainbow was transient, fading after a few minutes.

words.def: a lack of interest or concern
words.ex: Voter apathy meant that few people showed up for the election.

words.def: to stop short and refuse to go on
words.ex: The horse began to balk at the edge of the muddy creek.

words.def: shockingly bad and deserving blame
words.ex: The kennel was in deplorable shape, with dirty cages and no water.

words.def: to spread through every part of something
words.ex: The smell of baking bread began to pervade the house.

words.def: bold and willing to take risks
words.ex: Her audacious plan was to sail around the world alone.

words.def: dull and lacking energy or excitement
words.ex: The team gave a lackluster effort and lost badly.

words.def: a mild or polite word used in place of a harsh or unpleasant one
words.ex: Calling a failed test a learning experience is a euphemism.

words.def: messy and not cared for, especially hair or clothes
words.ex: After the camping trip, his hair was unkempt and full of leaves.

words.def: very fussy about small details
words.ex: My persnickety aunt straightens every picture frame she passes.

words.def: to refuse an offer or a friendly act in a cold or rude way
words.ex: The cat would rebuff anyone who tried to pick her up.

words.def: thinking and talking about yourself too much
words.ex: The egotistic singer bragged about his voice in every interview.

words.def: a very deep crack or opening in the ground
words.ex: A narrow rope bridge stretched across the chasm.

words.def: left empty and falling apart
words.ex: A derelict boat lay rotting on the beach.

words.def: too satisfied with yourself to see danger or a need to improve
words.ex: After winning so easily, the team became complacent.

words.def: describing a trait that only shows when a living thing gets two copies of its gene
words.ex: In pea plants, wrinkled seeds are a recessive trait.

words.def: the act of officially approving an agreement or law
words.ex: The new treaty needed ratification by each country before it could take effect.

words.def: unable or unwilling to believe something
words.ex: She gave me an incredulous look when I said I had cleaned my room.

words.def: loud and harsh-sounding
words.ex: The raucous laughter from the next table made it hard to talk.

words.def: a reply that tries to prove an argument wrong
words.ex: The debater gave a sharp rebuttal to her opponent's point.

words.def: to give someone a lasting gift, such as a talent or a sum of money
words.ex: The Creator chose to endow every person with special gifts.

words.def: given or produced in large amounts
words.ex: She offered profuse thanks for the help.

words.def: a person who has a lower rank than someone else
words.ex: The manager trusted her subordinate to run the meeting.

words.def: done by accident, without meaning to
words.ex: Leaving the gate open was an inadvertent mistake.

words.def: a long, narrow crack in rock or ice
words.ex: Steam rose from a fissure in the side of the volcano.

words.def: one of the forms of an element that has a different number of neutrons
words.ex: Carbon-14 is an isotope that scientists use to find the age of old bones and wood.

words.def: to move around or hide in a sneaky way, often for a bad reason
words.ex: A fox will skulk near the henhouse at night.

words.def: to stop resisting and give in
words.ex: After hours of pleading, Mom decided to capitulate and let us stay up.

words.def: impossible to prove wrong
words.ex: The video was irrefutable proof that the ball crossed the line.

words.def: producing a lot of money or profit
words.ex: Selling snacks at the stadium can be a lucrative job.

words.def: to travel across or through an area
words.ex: It took two days to traverse the mountain range.

words.def: messy and careless in appearance or work
words.ex: His slovenly handwriting was hard to read.

words.def: the quality of using few words or lasting a short time
words.ex: The audience appreciated the brevity of the principal's speech.

words.def: a large number of people or things arriving at once
words.ex: The beach town gets an influx of visitors every summer.

words.def: always accurate, never making a mistake
words.ex: The archer hit the target with unerring aim.

words.def: paying no attention to warnings or danger
words.ex: Heedless of the signs, the hikers left the trail.

words.def: the kind of cell division that makes reproductive cells
words.ex: Meiosis creates cells with only half the normal number of chromosomes.

words.def: to make something less harsh or serious
words.ex: Planting trees can help mitigate the summer heat in cities.

words.def: lying stretched out face down on the ground
words.ex: The worshippers lay prostrate before the altar.

words.def: to cancel something so that it has no effect
words.ex: Opening the sealed box will nullify the warranty.

words.def: a collection of writings by different authors in one book
words.ex: Our class anthology includes poems from every student.

words.def: one of the different forms of a gene that can produce different traits
words.ex: One allele for flower color makes petals purple, and another makes them white.

words.def: a person who does not follow common customs or beliefs
words.ex: As a nonconformist, he wore a top hat to school every day.

words.def: so interested that you pay complete attention
words.ex: The children listened with rapt attention to the story.

words.def: puzzled and confused, sometimes in an amused way
words.ex: The bemused tourist turned the map around three times.

words.def: a story that is longer than a short story but shorter than a novel
words.ex: She finished the novella in one afternoon.

words.def: to settle an argument by acting as a neutral judge whose decision both sides accept
words.ex: Both teams agreed to let the league arbitrate the dispute and accept whatever it decided.

words.def: a feeling of annoyance or frustration
words.ex: To her vexation, the bus pulled away just as she reached the stop.

words.def: a time of great trouble or suffering
words.ex: Through every tribulation, the church family stood together and prayed.

words.def: to shock someone because something is so bad or wrong
words.ex: The cruel treatment of the animals will appall anyone who sees it.

words.def: to pass by, as time does
words.ex: Three hours will elapse before the bread is ready.

words.def: having two separate lawmaking houses
words.ex: The United States has a bicameral Congress with a Senate and a House.

words.def: to look at someone with an angry stare
words.ex: The old man would glower at kids who cut across his lawn.

words.def: to keep bothering someone with lasting bitterness
words.ex: Losing the race by one second continued to rankle her for weeks.

words.def: to hold someone so spellbound that they cannot look away
words.ex: Good storytellers enthrall their listeners.

words.def: enjoying the company of other people; sociable
words.ex: My gregarious sister talks to everyone at the party.

words.def: to show great joy because of a success
words.ex: The fans began to exult when the final buzzer sounded.

words.def: to shut someone out of a group on purpose
words.ex: The book shows how hurtful it is to ostracize a classmate.

words.def: giving human traits to animals, objects or gods
words.ex: The anthropomorphic teapot in the cartoon sings and dances.

words.def: very carefully and gently, so as not to hurt anything
words.ex: I gingerly picked up the baby bird.

words.def: easily annoyed and grumpy
words.ex: The tired toddler grew peevish long before dinner.

words.def: to describe someone as wicked or evil, often unfairly
words.ex: The rival's posters tried to vilify the candidate as a cruel and dangerous liar.
